entries.title: The whole of the site copy rewritten and applied
entries.why: The language was stalling good companies. A reader who is told a business could not be confirmed hears that the business failed, and most of them had simply not been asked about.
entries.detail: 1,999 lines extracted to a copy register, rewritten, and applied back by whole node matching: 815 pairs replaced by node, 20 JavaScript fragments repaired by hand, 28 matched by similarity. Twenty verification gates repointed to the new wording.

report.x: What moved

Every text node, attribute and string literal on the site was extracted to a register of 1,999 lines with a stable reference against each one. The register was rewritten and applied back against those references, matching whole nodes only.

An earlier pass matched on substrings and injected short lines inside longer sentences. It was caught in the fix log, reverted from backup, and rewritten to require whole node, whole attribute or whole literal boundaries.
House rules applied on top
Every em dash and en dash replaced with a comma, a colon or a full stop.
Ranges written with the word to, never a dash.
Eight rendered uses of the word problem replaced.
not just replaced with not only throughout.
What could not be confirmed
protocheck could not run: it loads a prototype file that is not in the repository. Reported as an environment gap, not a regression.

entries.title: The line changed to Check before you send
entries.why: Know before you send promised knowledge. The product produces a check, and the two are not the same promise.
entries.detail: Renamed in the page title, the meta description, the panel label and both pack templates. Six verification gates repointed.

report.x: The wording appears in five places and all five moved together. A gate now fails the build if any one of them drifts from the others.

entries.title: Terms moved to version 1.1, dated 29 September 2026
entries.why: The clickwrap has to name the version a reader agreed to, and the version had not moved with the copy.
entries.detail: TERMS_VERSION set to 1.1 and TERMS_DATE to 29 September 2026. Stamped on the agreement record.

report.x: The version and the date are printed on the agreement record, so a reader can be shown which text they accepted.
OPEN: counsel has not reviewed version 1.1. It is recorded here as outstanding.

entries.title: A register that would have cleared a company, and was never asked
entries.why: A check on a Canadian crypto exchange told a consumer we could not confirm this business on a relevant register. The Ontario Securities Commission publishes the list of crypto asset trading platforms it has granted relief to, that company is on it as a Restricted Dealer, and the list was not in our catalogue, so it could not be asked.
entries.detail: OSC_CATP added to the catalogue at source tier A, category 02, marked link_out_only on the OSC's own terms. The register router now tells the OSC's two lists apart by path, so a registration list is never read as a warning list.

report.x: What happened

A consumer checking a registered Canadian dealer was shown three things: a foreign regulator's warning about a different company, one unhappy review, and the sentence that we could not confirm the business on a relevant register. Every one of the three was a separate fault and the sum of them was a false picture of a registered firm.
The record

The Ontario Securities Commission publishes, on its Crypto Businesses page, the platforms that have received exemptive relief to offer crypto products in Ontario, with each one's registration category and the date of its most recent decision. Newton Crypto Ltd. is listed there as a Restricted Dealer, dated 12 March 2025.
Why it could not be read

The list was not in the catalogue. A register that is not in the catalogue is never asked, and a register that is never asked returns nothing, and nothing was being reported to a consumer as an absence of registration rather than as a gap in our own reading.
What was done
OSC_CATP added at source tier A, in category 02 registration and licensing, also credited to category 01.

Marked link_out_only. The OSC's terms bar commercial use of their content, so the fact of an entry is ours to report in our own words with the date and the link, and their text is not ours to publish.
The register router now separates the OSC's registration pages from its alert pages by path, so the two can never be read as each other.
What could not be confirmed

Permission has not been requested from the OSC. Until it is, this register can be pointed at and not reproduced, which is a weaker check than it needs to be. Asking is the whole of the fix and it is open.

entries.title: The favourable side of the record, ranked by how hard it is to buy
entries.why: The engine only ever went looking for what was wrong. That is defensible on its own terms and it is also how a good business gets stalled, because a company with nothing against it and a great deal in its favour produced a page that said nothing at all.
entries.detail: New module ranking every favourable record into three: cannot be bought, expensive to fake, buyable. A new retrieval pass on the same platforms as the adverse one. A standing block in the output contract. Rank enforced in code against the model's own answer, lower of the two wins.

report.x: The one question
Favourable evidence is ranked by how hard it is to buy, and by nothing else.

rows: A live registration, a licence in good standing, a regulator's own record, a filed financial statement, a court record showing a matter resolved, an exchange listing
Nobody sells these. They are facts about standing, not opinions about service
Continuity rather than content: the same legal name across three registers, on the register since 2018, a domain eight years old, a filing history without gaps
Star ratings, review counts, testimonials, award badges, press releases

report.x: The rule that holds it up

Favourable evidence never changes the verdict. Register standing and adverse findings set the result. Everything else is context beside it. The standing block is computed after the verdict is settled and is never read back, and there is deliberately no code path from it to the verdict.

That is the defence against bought reviews, and it is cheaper and more reliable than any detector: once a purchased five star page has nowhere to move the needle, buying one stops working. It also has no false positives, which a detector would.
What the platforms say about themselves

Trustpilot removed 4.5 million reviews it had detected as fake in 2024. That is 7.4 per cent of everything submitted that year, up from 6.1 per cent in 2023, and it reports that 90 per cent of them were caught by its own automated detection.

Buying positive reviews, writing insider reviews without disclosing the connection, and using threats to get negative reviews taken down have all been unlawful in the United States since October 2024 under the Federal Trade Commission's final rule at 16 CFR Part 465.
What could not be confirmed

Trustpilot does not publish its weighting formula. Its public statement is that the score is weighted to reflect that newer reviews tend to be more relevant than older ones, with no thresholds given. We did not model it and we do not rely on it.

entries.title: The time window: a year drives the result, three years is the edge of the page
entries.why: Businesses make mistakes and then fix them. A fault from four years ago that was put right should not sit over a company for the rest of its life, and a consumer reading a result today is asking about today.
entries.detail: Four bands computed in code from the date the record carries: current inside 12 months drives the result, older at 12 to 36 months is shown and labelled, archive beyond 36 months sits behind one control, undated is routed to what we could not confirm. Standing is exempt by class and never ages.

report.x: The bands

rows: Behind one control the reader can open
Never a finding. Goes to what we could not confirm

report.x: Standing never ages

A register entry, a licence, a regulator action, a sanction and a court record describe what is true now until the issuing body changes them. A licence granted in 2019 is not stale, it is current. An enforcement order from 2021 that was never lifted is not history, it is the present state of that party's record. Ageing those out would be the single most dangerous thing this module could do, so they are exempt by class and can never fall into a band.
Why the arithmetic is not the model's

Published work on model based reranking found that injecting dates alone moved the mean publication year of the top ten forward by up to 4.78 years, moved single items as many as 95 ranks, and flipped pairwise preferences between equally relevant passages by up to 25 per cent. Larger models reduced the effect and none eliminated it.
So the model carries the date and does not weigh it. The band is computed from the date, in code, where it is arithmetic and does not have that failure.
A date we cannot read

An ambiguous numeric date is read as the later of its two possible readings, and a bare year as the last day of it. Reading a date as newer than it is can only make a record count more than it should, which is the conservative direction for a favourable record and the safe one for an adverse one.
What could not be confirmed

The window only works where the source carries a date. A source that publishes undated material produces undated records, and those are now named as gaps rather than counted. How large that population is has not been measured on live traffic.

entries.title: A category may no longer stay red on records older than a year
entries.why: The attachment rule reached the verdict and the time window did not. A page could be held red by a single aged incident about a business that had already fixed it.
entries.detail: A red category with no record that both names the party and falls inside the current band comes down to yellow, and the reason is written into the payload. Standing is exempt, so a live enforcement action still holds a page red whatever its date.

report.x: The demotion is recorded in the payload rather than applied silently, so the back office can count how often it fires and see what it fired on.

Two separate demotions now run in sequence. The first is the attachment rule: a red category with no record naming the party comes down. The second is the window: a red category whose only records naming the party are older than a year comes down.
Undated evidence about the party is appended to what we could not confirm, named by source, rather than being printed as a finding it cannot support.

entries.title: The consumer language for all of it
entries.why: None of the above is worth building if the page does not say it in words a consumer reads once and understands.
entries.detail: The favourable block now carries a rank chip on every record, a note on anything purchasable, a band label on anything older than a year, a separate quoted block for the business's own words, a shape note on the good reviews where two or more signals agree, and one control for records older than three years.

report.x: What the reader now sees
Every favourable record wears the rank it earned: Cannot be bought, Expensive to fake, or Can be bought.
Anything purchasable carries the line that ratings, testimonials and badges can be paid for, that we show them and do not count them.
The business's own words sit in their own block, quoted and attributed, under the line that a business saying something about itself is not evidence that it is true.
Where two or more shape signals agree, the page says what the pile looks like and says plainly that we are not calling any single review false.
One control opens everything older than three years, with the count on the button and the reason under it.
What the page may never do
There is no tally anywhere. A consumer shown nine positive against three negative will do arithmetic on evidence of wildly different quality, which is the exact mistake this product exists to stop.

entries.title: The change register, and this page
entries.why: The only account of what had changed was a build number and whatever anybody remembered. That is the shape of file a regulator asks for and a company cannot produce.
entries.detail: docs/change-register.json is the source of truth, embedded into the control panel at build time. db/audit.sql is the runtime half. Every entry opens to a report.

report.x: The register is in the repository and reviewed like code. It is embedded rather than fetched, for the same two reasons the control documents are: this page is behind the gate and these are internal records, and the page has to read the same when it is opened as a file.
An entry with no reason is rejected. A change with no reason is not a record of anything.
Nothing in this register may carry an identifier anybody searched, a party a check was about, or a result a check returned. It is enforced on the write path, not asked for.

entries.title: Powered by 4orm Finance, on both screens
entries.why: The only route from the consumer product to the house was a bare domain sitting in the row of standing documents, where it read as a legal notice. The site footer carried no route at all.
entries.detail: A small Powered by 4orm Finance line on the landing screen and in the site footer. The name itself is the link and it opens in a new tab. The footer label moved to 4ormIQ so the house is not named twice on one screen, and the missing separator before Terms of use was restored in both rows.

report.x: Where it sits
Landing screen, centred, under the standing documents rather than inside them. A company link is not a legal notice and sitting in that row made it read as one.
Site footer, which until now carried no route to the house at all.
The decisions behind it

The name itself is the link. A name sitting beside a second control that repeats the name is the tell of an amateur page, and this line is far too small to carry one. The accessible label carries Check out 4orm Finance for anyone reading it with assistive technology, and the same words are the hover title.

It opens in a new tab on purpose. A consumer part way through a check who taps this and loses their page has been sent away by us at the one moment they came to us for help. That is a worse outcome than never carrying the link at all.
The footer named the house at the top and would now have named it again three rows down. The label reads 4ormIQ instead, which is the product a reader is actually standing in.
Two gates it tripped, and what they caught
The words Powered by at the faintest ink measured 3.94 against the page, under the 4.5 floor. They take the same ink the standing document row already uses. Size and tracking did not move.
The layout duplication scanner reads comment text as part of a selector, so a comma in a code comment above the rule produced a false clash. The comment was rewritten without it.
What is deliberately not here

Nothing was added to the result page. A consumer reading a result about a business they are worried about is not the audience for a company link, and putting one there would be the wrong thing at the wrong moment.

entries.title: The landing body, three weights instead of four paragraphs
entries.why: Between the headline and the search box sat four stacked paragraphs, nine lines, nearly all of it at the same size, weight and ink. A reader got four headlines in a row and no way to tell which to read first, and the one thing they came to do was underneath all of it.
entries.detail: The question leads, the promise drops to body copy, the limit is quieter again. The note that says how to type an identifier moved from above the box to under the field. More air above the box. No words cut, no type sizes reduced, headline and search box untouched.

report.x: What was wrong

The question, the promise and the limit were all set at the same size, the same weight and the same ink, so the hierarchy that should have been doing the work was being asked of the words instead. Under them sat a third paragraph at the site's hero lead size whose actual job is telling somebody how to type an identifier.
What changed
The question keeps the lead size and weight. It is the line that tells a reader whether this page is for them.
The promise becomes body copy under it: lighter weight, the body ink, a 62 character measure.
The limit is quieter again, at the size of a qualification rather than a claim, balanced so it does not drop its last word onto a row of its own.
The note about how to type an identifier moved below the search field and took the size of help. Help for a control belongs with the control.
The gap above the search box went from 26 to 40, so the box reads as the action rather than as a fifth paragraph.
On a phone the three gaps close, because the change in size and ink already separates them in a column that narrow.
What did not change
The headline, the search box, every word on the screen and every type size in the block above it. The crowding was hierarchy, not volume, and the fix is hierarchy.
Measured
At 1440 the search box now sits at 548 of 900 and the note at 655. At 390 the box sits at 448 of 844. Both are clear of the fold, which is the measurement that governs this block.
A gate that was reading the wrong rule

The build check for this note took the first rule naming its selector, which after the change was a phone breakpoint setting only a margin, and reported the size as missing. It reads every rule naming the selector now.
What is still open
On a phone the promise still runs to four lines and the question to three. That is sentence length rather than layout, and shortening either one is a copy decision that has not been taken.
